title: Best Hosting for WordPress
description: Hosting ranked for WordPress-specific needs: PHP workers, caching, and plugin compatibility.
intro: WordPress is PHP-based, so the best hosts optimize specifically for PHP-FPM workers, object caching, and page-level caching. Kinsta and WP Engine are purpose-built for it; Hostinger and SiteGround offer the best value with LiteSpeed and SG Optimizer respectively.

keyFeatures.title: LiteSpeed / Varnish Caching
keyFeatures.text: Built-in page and object caching for faster WordPress rendering.

keyFeatures.title: PHP 8.x + MariaDB
keyFeatures.text: Optimized PHP workers and database tuning out of the box.

keyFeatures.title: WordPress-Specific Security
keyFeatures.text: WAF, malware scanning, and auto-updates handled by the host.

faqs.question: What is the best hosting for WordPress?
faqs.answer: Kinsta is the overall performance winner, but Hostinger is the best value. Cloudways is ideal for developers who want cloud infrastructure with a managed WordPress layer.

faqs.question: Should I choose shared or managed WordPress hosting?
faqs.answer: For hobby and most business sites, premium shared hosting (Hostinger, SiteGround) is enough. For high-traffic or revenue-critical sites, managed hosting (Kinsta, WP Engine) is worth the premium.

faqs.question: What hosting specs does WordPress need?
faqs.answer: At minimum 1 CPU core, 1GB RAM, NVMe/SSD storage, PHP 8.x, and a caching layer. 10GB+ NVMe storage handles most sites comfortably.

title: Best Hosting for Next.js
description: Next.js hosting benchmarked on SSR response, ISR invalidation, and edge latency.
intro: Next.js needs more than a static host. Vercel - as the framework's creator - delivers native App Router, Server Actions, ISR, and Edge middleware support. Cloudflare Pages and Vercel offer edge rendering; DigitalOcean and Vultr give you full control on a VPS with Nginx + PM2.

keyFeatures.title: Sub-50ms SSR
keyFeatures.text: Optimized compute for Server-Side Rendering response times.

keyFeatures.title: Instant ISR
keyFeatures.text: Global cache invalidation for Incremental Static Regeneration.

keyFeatures.title: Edge Functions
keyFeatures.text: Deploy middleware and functions globally with minimal latency.

faqs.question: What is the best hosting for Next.js?
faqs.answer: Vercel is the best overall - it's created by the Next.js team and natively supports every framework feature. Cloudflare Pages is the best free alternative, and a VPS (DigitalOcean/Vultr) is best when you need custom infrastructure.

faqs.question: Can I host Next.js for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Vercel's Hobby plan and Cloudflare Pages both offer free tiers that handle significant traffic, including App Router projects with edge rendering.

faqs.question: Should I deploy Next.js on a VPS instead?
faqs.answer: A VPS gives you full control and predictable costs at scale, but you handle Node.js process management (PM2), reverse proxying (Nginx), and SSL yourself. See our tutorial for a step-by-step setup.

title: Best Hosting for Node.js
description: Node.js hosting compared on process management, clustering, and scaling.
intro: Node.js apps need hosts that handle long-running processes, clustering, and WebSockets. Platform services like Vercel and Cloudflare Pages manage the runtime for you; VPS providers like DigitalOcean and Vultr give you full control with PM2 clustering.

keyFeatures.title: Native Runtime
keyFeatures.text: Node.js LTS versions with proper process supervision.

keyFeatures.title: Clustering & WebSockets
keyFeatures.text: Horizontal scaling and real-time connections supported.

keyFeatures.title: Predictable RAM
keyFeatures.text: Isolated memory guarantees for long-running processes.

faqs.question: What is the best Node.js hosting?
faqs.answer: For full control, DigitalOcean and Vultr droplets are the developer favorites. For zero-config deploys, Vercel and Cloudflare Pages run Node.js functions at the edge. Cloudways adds a managed layer on top of cloud VMs.

faqs.question: How much RAM does a Node.js app need?
faqs.answer: A small API needs 512MB-1GB RAM. Production apps with a database typically want 2GB+. Choose a plan with room to grow - Node.js memory usage is notoriously hard to predict.

faqs.question: Is Node.js hosting different from web hosting?
faqs.answer: Yes. Traditional shared hosting runs PHP/WordPress and can't run Node.js processes. You need a VPS, PaaS, or a platform like Vercel that supports Node.js runtimes.

title: Best Hosting for Python
description: Python hosting for Django, Flask, and FastAPI apps - benchmarked for cold starts and throughput.
intro: Python apps (Django, Flask, FastAPI) are best served by platforms or VPS instances with clean process management. We benchmarked cold-start times and request throughput for Python workloads across every major provider.

keyFeatures.title: Python 3.x Runtimes
keyFeatures.text: Recent Python versions with pip/venv support out of the box.

keyFeatures.title: Low Cold Starts
keyFeatures.text: Fast function and container cold starts for API workloads.

keyFeatures.title: Managed Databases
keyFeatures.text: PostgreSQL and MySQL options for Django and FastAPI apps.

faqs.question: What is the best Python hosting?
faqs.answer: For Django/FastAPI with full control, DigitalOcean droplets are the developer favorite. Vercel supports Python serverless functions for APIs. Cloudways provides managed Python servers for teams that want less DevOps.

faqs.question: Is Python hosting expensive?
faqs.answer: No. A $4-6/mo VPS runs Django fine for moderate traffic. Serverless Python functions have free tiers but scale with usage.

faqs.question: Can I host Django on shared hosting?
faqs.answer: Rarely - most shared hosts only run PHP. For Django or Flask, you need a VPS, PaaS (Render, Railway), or a cloud platform.

title: Best Hosting for Laravel
description: Laravel hosting with PHP-FPM, Redis queues, and Horizon support.
intro: Laravel applications need PHP 8.2+, Redis for queues and caching, and proper workers. Cloudways is the standout managed option with one-click Laravel apps; DigitalOcean and Vultr are the strongest DIY choices.

keyFeatures.title: PHP 8.x + Composer
keyFeatures.text: Modern PHP runtimes with Composer dependency support.

keyFeatures.title: Redis + Queues
keyFeatures.text: Redis for cache and queue drivers, with Horizon-ready workers.

keyFeatures.title: SSH + CLI Access
keyFeatures.text: Full terminal access for artisan commands and deployments.

faqs.question: What is the best Laravel hosting?
faqs.answer: Cloudways is our top pick for managed Laravel hosting - one-click deploys with Redis and Varnish. DigitalOcean is the best unmanaged alternative for teams that want full control.

faqs.question: Can I run Laravel on shared hosting?
faqs.answer: Technically yes, but it's painful - you need SSH, Composer, Redis, and queue workers. A VPS or managed cloud is strongly recommended.

faqs.question: What server specs does Laravel need?
faqs.answer: 2GB RAM is a comfortable starting point with PHP-FPM tuned workers, OpCache enabled, and Redis handling cache/queues. NVMe storage keeps artisan and composer operations fast.

title: Best Hosting for Docker
description: Docker and containerized workloads - from raw VPS to container platforms.
intro: Containerized apps give you portable, reproducible deployments. DigitalOcean's App Platform and Droplets with Docker, Vultr's optimized compute, and Cloudways' container-ready cloud are our top recommendations for Docker workloads.

keyFeatures.title: Docker Native
keyFeatures.text: Pre-installed Docker and docker-compose support.

keyFeatures.title: Container Orchestration
keyFeatures.text: Scale containers horizontally as your traffic grows.

keyFeatures.title: Isolated Environments
keyFeatures.text: Container isolation for secure multi-app hosting.

faqs.question: What is the best Docker hosting?
faqs.answer: DigitalOcean (Droplets or App Platform) is the developer favorite for Docker. Vultr matches it on raw price with high-frequency compute. Cloudflare Workers containers and Pages Functions handle containerized workloads at the edge.

faqs.question: Can I run Docker on shared hosting?
faqs.answer: No. Docker requires a VPS, cloud VM, or container platform. You need root access to install the Docker engine.

faqs.question: How much RAM does Docker need?
faqs.answer: Each container consumes 128MB-512MB typically. For a few containers, 2GB is fine; for production stacks with databases, plan for 4GB+.

title: Best Hosting for AI Websites
h1: Best Hosting for AI Websites in 2025
description: Infrastructure for AI apps - GPU-adjacent compute, vector databases, and WebSockets.
intro: AI applications need streaming responses, WebSocket support, generous egress bandwidth, and often vector database access. Edge platforms handle streaming beautifully, while VPS providers give you the compute headroom for embedding generation and inference proxies.

keyFeatures.title: Streaming Responses
keyFeatures.text: Native support for SSE and WebSocket streaming.

keyFeatures.title: Vector Database Ready
keyFeatures.text: Support for pgvector, Pinecone, and other vector stores.

keyFeatures.title: High Egress Bandwidth
keyFeatures.text: Generous bandwidth for model responses and embeddings.

faqs.question: What is the best hosting for AI websites?
faqs.answer: Vercel excels at streaming AI app frontends with edge rendering. Vultr and DigitalOcean provide the compute and bandwidth for embedding pipelines and inference. Cloudflare's edge network handles global delivery with free bandwidth.

faqs.question: Do AI apps need GPUs?
faqs.answer: Only if you run inference yourself. Most AI websites call hosted models (OpenAI, Anthropic) and just need fast streaming, WebSockets, and a vector database - no GPU required.

faqs.question: How much bandwidth do AI apps use?
faqs.answer: Chat-based apps can be bandwidth-heavy due to token streaming. Choose hosts with generous egress (Cloudflare's free tier includes unlimited) or budget carefully.

title: Best Hosting for n8n
description: Where to self-host n8n for reliable, always-on automation workflows.
intro: n8n is a workflow automation tool best self-hosted for unlimited executions and data privacy. It's a Node.js app that runs great on a small VPS with Docker. DigitalOcean and Vultr droplets are the most popular homes for n8n deployments.

keyFeatures.title: Always-On Uptime
keyFeatures.text: Scheduled and webhook-triggered workflows need reliable processes.

keyFeatures.title: Docker Deploys
keyFeatures.text: Official n8n Docker image for quick, reproducible installs.

keyFeatures.title: Persistent Storage
keyFeatures.text: Dedicated volumes keep workflow history and credentials safe.

faqs.question: What is the best hosting for n8n?
faqs.answer: A DigitalOcean or Vultr droplet with 2GB RAM running n8n in Docker is the community standard. Cloudways offers managed servers if you want less DevOps overhead.

faqs.question: How much RAM does n8n need?
faqs.answer: n8n runs comfortably in 1-2GB RAM for moderate workloads. Heavy workflow concurrency benefits from 4GB and a proper database (PostgreSQL) instead of SQLite.

faqs.question: Should I self-host n8n or use the cloud version?
faqs.answer: Self-hosting is unlimited and cheaper long-term, plus your credentials stay on your server. The cloud version is faster to start but execution limits and pricing add up.
